newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner wins stake in Sakhalin deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner wins stake in Sakhalin deal.

text.p: Norwegian industrial group Kvaerner ASA said on Friday it had won a 12-15 percent stake in a $1 billion contract to build a production platform in the Arkutun Dagi field off Sakhalin island in eastern Russia.
"Kvaerner's share will be about 12-15 percent," a Kvaerner spokeswoman said.
A Kvaerner statement said the contract embraced project management, engineering, procurement and construction management for the platform's jacket and topsides.

"Emphasis will be placed on the use of Russian equipment suppliers and fabrication yards for the project. The total installed cost for this project is about $1 billion. The project execution team will be located in London," it said.

Plans call for a fixed jacket supporting a 20,000-30,000 tonne topside with drilling equipment, processing facilities and living quarters. The platform is expected to have a daily capacity of 115,000 barrels of oil and 360 million cubic feet of gas.
"We're very pleased that the Sakhalin 1 Consortium has shown us this confidence," Kvaerner executive vice president Tore Bergersen said.

"The contract was won in strong international competition and proved that our technology and capabilities are among the world's best. Our extensive experience with major offshore projects played a key role in this selection, and will unquestionably help us a lot with the work."

Operator Exxon Neftegas Ltd has a 30 per cent interest in the field, Russia's Rosneft-Sakhalin and Sakhalinmorneftegas-Shelf have 17 and 23 per cent respectively and the Japanese Sakhalin Oil and Gas Development Co Ltd (SODECO) has 30 per cent.
